test_case_title: FastAPI - Create item for registered user
test_case_steps: Register a new user; authenticate with that user's credentials; create an item with a title and description.
expected_behavior: HTTP 200; returned title and description match the request; an item id is present; owner_id matches the registered user.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Read item by ID as superuser
test_case_steps: Authenticate as the superuser; create an item; retrieve that item by its returned id.
expected_behavior: HTTP 200; returned title, description, id, and owner_id match the created item.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as the superuser; request an item using an id that does not exist.
expected_behavior: HTTP 404 with detail 'Item not found'.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Prevent reading another user's item
test_case_steps: Register two normal users; user A creates an item; user B attempts to retrieve user A's item.
expected_behavior: HTTP 400 with detail 'Not enough permissions'.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as the superuser; create two items; request the item list.
expected_behavior: HTTP 200 and the returned collection contains at least both newly created items.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as the superuser; create an item; update its title and description.
expected_behavior: HTTP 200; title and description are updated while id and owner_id remain those of the original item.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as the superuser; attempt to update an item using a nonexistent id.
expected_behavior: HTTP 404 with detail 'Item not found'.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Prevent updating another user's item
test_case_steps: Register two normal users; user A creates an item; user B attempts to update user A's item.
expected_behavior: HTTP 400 with detail 'Not enough permissions'.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as the superuser; create an item; delete that item.
expected_behavior: HTTP 200 with message 'Item deleted successfully'.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as the superuser; attempt to delete an item using a nonexistent id.
expected_behavior: HTTP 404 with detail 'Item not found'.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Prevent deleting another user's item
test_case_steps: Register two normal users; user A creates an item; user B attempts to delete user A's item.
expected_behavior: HTTP 400 with detail 'Not enough permissions'.

test_case_steps: Authenticate using the configured superuser credentials.
expected_behavior: HTTP 200; access_token is present and non-empty; token_type is 'bearer'.

test_case_steps: Register a user; attempt to log in with the correct email and an incorrect password.
expected_behavior: HTTP 400 and authentication fails.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as the superuser; call the access-token test endpoint with the returned token.
expected_behavior: HTTP 200 and the response identifies the superuser email as admin@example.com.

test_case_steps: Register a normal user; request password recovery for that email; inspect the mail-catcher service.
expected_behavior: HTTP 200 with message 'Password recovery email sent', and a recovery email is captured by the mail service.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Reject recovery for nonexistent user
test_case_steps: Request password recovery for an email that is not registered.
expected_behavior: HTTP 404.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Reset password with recovery token
test_case_steps: Create a user; authenticate as superuser; obtain the user's password-recovery HTML/token; submit a reset request with a new password.
expected_behavior: HTTP 200 with message 'Password updated successfully'.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as the superuser; submit a password-reset request using an invalid reset token.
expected_behavior: HTTP 400 with detail 'Invalid token'.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Create and retrieve user by ID
test_case_steps: Create a user through the private user-creation operation; authenticate as superuser; retrieve the created user by its returned id.
expected_behavior: Creation and retrieval return HTTP 200; retrieved email and full_name match the created user.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as the superuser; retrieve the current-user profile.
expected_behavior: Response body is non-empty; is_active is true; is_superuser is true; email matches the configured superuser.

test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a normal user; retrieve the current-user profile.
expected_behavior: Response body is non-empty; is_active is true; is_superuser is false; email matches the registered user.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as the superuser; create a new user with a generated email and password.
expected_behavior: Successful 2xx response; returned email matches; id is present; is_active is true.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Retrieve user by ID as superuser
test_case_steps: Register a normal user; authenticate as superuser; retrieve that user by id.
expected_behavior: Successful 2xx response; returned email and id match the registered user and is_active is true.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Retrieve own user by ID
test_case_steps: Register a normal user; log in; retrieve that user's record by its id using the user's token.
expected_behavior: Successful 2xx response; returned email and id match the authenticated user.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Prevent normal user reading another user
test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a normal user; request a different/random user id.
expected_behavior: HTTP 403 with detail indicating the user does not have enough privileges.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as superuser; create a user; attempt to create another user using the same email and password.
expected_behavior: Second creation returns HTTP 400 and does not return an _id field.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Prevent normal user creating users
test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a normal user; attempt to call the privileged create-user operation.
expected_behavior: HTTP 403.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as superuser; create two distinct users; retrieve the user list.
expected_behavior: HTTP 200; response contains data and count; both newly created users appear in the data collection.

test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a normal user; update the current user's email and full name.
expected_behavior: HTTP 200; returned email and full_name equal the submitted new values.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as superuser; change the current password to a new password; verify login with the new password; restore the original password and log in again.
expected_behavior: Both password updates return HTTP 200 with success message; login succeeds with the active password after each change.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Register valid user and login
test_case_steps: Generate valid email, password, and full name; register the user; then log in with the generated credentials.
expected_behavior: Registration returns HTTP 200 with matching email and full_name; subsequent login succeeds.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Reject registration with existing email
test_case_steps: Attempt to register a new account using the already configured superuser email.
expected_behavior: HTTP 400 with detail stating that a user with the email already exists.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Update user by ID as superuser
test_case_steps: Register a normal user; authenticate as superuser; update that user's full_name by id; retrieve the user again.
expected_behavior: Update returns HTTP 200 with the new full_name, and the value remains changed when the user is re-fetched.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as superuser; attempt to update a user identified by a generated UUID that does not exist.
expected_behavior: HTTP 404 with detail indicating that the user id does not exist.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Reject changing user email to existing email
test_case_steps: Register two users; authenticate as superuser; attempt to change the first user's email to the second user's email.
expected_behavior: HTTP 409 with detail 'User with this email already exists'.

test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a normal user; delete the current user's account; then attempt to log in again.
expected_behavior: Deletion returns HTTP 200 with message 'User deleted successfully'; login with the deleted credentials fails.

test_case_steps: Authenticate as the configured superuser; attempt to delete the current user's own account.
expected_behavior: HTTP 403 with detail 'Super users are not allowed to delete themselves'.

test_case_steps: Register a normal user; authenticate as superuser; delete the registered user by id; attempt to log in as the deleted user.
expected_behavior: Delete returns HTTP 200 with success message; login for the deleted user fails with HTTP 400.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Delete nonexistent user by ID
test_case_steps: Authenticate as superuser; attempt to delete a user using a random UUID that does not exist.
expected_behavior: HTTP 404 with detail 'User not found'.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Prevent deleting current superuser by ID
test_case_steps: Authenticate as superuser; obtain the current superuser id; attempt to delete that same id.
expected_behavior: HTTP 403 with detail 'Super users are not allowed to delete themselves'.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Prevent normal user deleting another user
test_case_steps: Register two normal users; authenticate as user A; attempt to delete user B by id; verify user B can still log in.
expected_behavior: Deletion returns HTTP 403 with insufficient-privileges detail, and user B remains active.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Cascade item deletion after admin deletes user
test_case_steps: Register a normal user; create an item as that user; authenticate as superuser and delete the user; then retrieve the item by id.
expected_behavior: User deletion returns HTTP 200; the former user's item is no longer available and retrieval returns HTTP 404.

test_case_title: FastAPI - Cascade item deletion after self-delete
test_case_steps: Register a normal user; create an item; delete the user's own account; authenticate as superuser and request the former item.
expected_behavior: Self-deletion returns HTTP 200; the former user's item retrieval returns HTTP 404.

test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a user; attempt to update the current profile to a malformed email address.
expected_behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

test_case_steps: Create a user with username, email, and password; obtain the returned token; retrieve the current user with that token.
expected_behavior: Creation returns HTTP 201 with matching username/email and a token; current-user retrieval returns HTTP 200 with the same account data.

test_case_title: RealWorld - Follow user and prevent self-follow
test_case_steps: Create two users; have user A follow user B; retrieve B's profile as A; then have A attempt to follow itself.
expected_behavior: Following B returns HTTP 200 and following=true; the profile remains marked followed; self-follow is rejected with HTTP 400.

test_case_title: RealWorld - Create article and resolve slug
test_case_steps: Create and authenticate a user; create an article with title, description, body, and tags; retrieve it using the returned slug.
expected_behavior: Creation returns HTTP 201; fields and tags are preserved; slug starts with the normalized title; retrieval by slug returns HTTP 200 with the article.

test_case_title: RealWorld - Update article while preserving slug
test_case_steps: Create a user and article; update the article title and description using the original slug; retrieve it again by that slug.
expected_behavior: Update returns HTTP 200 with new values, and retrieval via the original slug returns the updated article.

test_case_steps: Create a user and article; confirm the article can be retrieved; delete it by slug; attempt retrieval again.
expected_behavior: Deletion returns HTTP 200 and the article is no longer retrievable successfully.

test_case_title: RealWorld - Feed contains only followed authors
test_case_steps: Create a reader and two authors; each author creates an article; check the reader's feed before following anyone; follow one author and check the feed again.
expected_behavior: Initial feed contains no articles; after following one author, the feed contains that author's article and excludes the unfollowed author's article.

test_case_title: RealWorld - Add and retrieve article comment
test_case_steps: Create a user and article; add a comment to the article; retrieve the article comments.
expected_behavior: Comment creation returns HTTP 200; the comment is retrievable with the expected body and has a numeric id.

test_case_steps: Create a user, article, and comment; delete the comment by id; retrieve the article's comments again.
expected_behavior: Deletion returns HTTP 200 and the deleted comment is absent from the comments collection.

test_case_title: RealWorld - Reject duplicate username or email
test_case_steps: Create a user; attempt another registration with the same username but different email; then another with different username but the same email.
expected_behavior: Both duplicate attempts return HTTP 400 with a uniqueness error.

test_case_title: RealWorld - Unfollow user and prevent self-unfollow
test_case_steps: Create two users; have user A follow user B; then unfollow B and retrieve B's profile; finally attempt to unfollow A itself.
expected_behavior: Unfollow returns HTTP 200 and following=false; profile remains unfollowed; self-unfollow is rejected with HTTP 400.

test_case_steps: Create a user; log in once with the correct password and once with an incorrect password.
expected_behavior: Correct login returns HTTP 201 with matching user data and a valid token; wrong-password login returns HTTP 401.

test_case_steps: Create a user and three articles with overlapping and distinct tags; query articles by several tag values.
expected_behavior: Each tag filter returns only matching articles; a nonexistent tag yields zero matching articles.

test_case_steps: Create two authors and one article per author; query articles separately by each author and once without an author filter.
expected_behavior: Each author query returns only that author's article; the unfiltered query contains both articles.

test_case_title: RealWorld - Update profile bio and image
test_case_steps: Create and authenticate a user; update bio and image through the current-user endpoint; retrieve the user again.
expected_behavior: Update returns HTTP 200 with the submitted bio/image and a later retrieval shows the values persisted.

test_case_steps: Create five articles; request the article list with limit=2, then limit=2 with offset=2, then a limit larger than the dataset.
expected_behavior: Pagination respects limit and offset; total count remains 5; the large-limit request returns all five articles.

test_case_title: RealWorld - Reflect follow status in profile
test_case_steps: Create two users; inspect target profile before following; follow the target and inspect again; unfollow and inspect a third time.
expected_behavior: following changes false -> true -> false while the target username remains correct.

test_case_title: RealWorld - Associate articles with correct author
test_case_steps: Create two users; each creates one article; request articles filtered by each username.
expected_behavior: Each author filter returns exactly the article created by that author and excludes the other author's article.

test_case_steps: Create one article with three tags and another with an empty tag list; retrieve both by slug.
expected_behavior: The first article returns exactly the three stored tags as an array; the second returns an empty tag array.

test_case_steps: Create an article and record created/updated timestamps; wait briefly; update the article; retrieve it again.
expected_behavior: created remains unchanged and updated becomes newer than its original value.

test_case_steps: Create two articles with the same title under the same user and capture both generated slugs.
expected_behavior: Both creations succeed; slugs share the normalized title prefix but are different because of their suffixes.

test_case_title: RealWorld - Persist article title and description
test_case_steps: Create an article with a known title and description; retrieve it by slug.
expected_behavior: Retrieved title and description exactly match the values supplied at creation.

test_case_title: RealWorld - Return profile bio and image
test_case_steps: Create a user; set a known bio and image; retrieve the public profile by username.
expected_behavior: Profile returns the correct username, bio, and image.

test_case_steps: Create reader and author; reader follows author; author creates five articles; request feed with limit=2 and then limit=2&offset=2.
expected_behavior: Feed reports total count 5 while returning two items per page; the offset request returns a different page.

test_case_steps: Create three articles separated by short delays; retrieve the global article list.
expected_behavior: Articles are ordered by creation timestamp descending, with newest articles first.

test_case_steps: Create a user; decode the payload of the returned JWT; also use the token to retrieve the current user.
expected_behavior: JWT payload contains the correct user id, username, and email; authenticated user retrieval matches the same account.

test_case_title: RealWorld - Store multiple comments with unique IDs
test_case_steps: Create a user and article; add three comments with distinct bodies; retrieve all comments for the article.
expected_behavior: Three comments are returned; each has a unique id and each original comment body is preserved.

test_case_title: TodoApp - List only current user's todos
test_case_steps: Register two users; each creates a different todo; user A requests GET /todos.
expected_behavior: The returned list contains user A's todo and does not expose user B's todo.

test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a user; attempt to create a todo with an empty or missing title.
expected_behavior: HTTP 400 Bad Request with validation-error details.

test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a user; create a todo; retrieve it using the returned id.
expected_behavior: The response contains the correct todo data for the created id.

test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a user; request a todo id that does not exist.
expected_behavior: HTTP 404 Not Found.

test_case_title: TodoApp - Prevent access to another user's todo
test_case_steps: Register users A and B; user A creates a todo; user B requests user A's todo id.
expected_behavior: HTTP 404 and user B cannot access user A's todo.

test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a user; create a todo; delete it by id; request the same id again.
expected_behavior: Deletion returns HTTP 200 and subsequent retrieval returns HTTP 404.

test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a user; attempt to delete a todo id that does not exist.
expected_behavior: HTTP 404 Not Found.

test_case_title: TodoApp - Prevent deleting another user's todo
test_case_steps: Register users A and B; user A creates a todo; user B attempts to delete that id; user A retrieves it afterward.
expected_behavior: User B receives HTTP 404 and user A's todo still exists.

test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a user; create an incomplete todo; update isComplete to true; retrieve it again.
expected_behavior: Update returns HTTP 200 and the retrieved todo has isComplete=true.

test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a user; create a todo with id X; call PUT /todos/X using a body whose id is Y.
expected_behavior: HTTP 400 Bad Request.

test_case_steps: Register and authenticate a user; submit a valid update for a todo id that does not exist.
expected_behavior: HTTP 404 Not Found.

test_case_title: TodoApp - Prevent updating another user's todo
test_case_steps: Register users A and B; user A creates a todo; user B attempts to update it; user A retrieves it afterward.
expected_behavior: User B receives HTTP 404 and user A's todo remains unchanged.

test_case_title: TodoApp - Register user with valid credentials
test_case_steps: Register a new user with a valid email and password.
expected_behavior: HTTP 200 and registration succeeds.

test_case_title: TodoApp - Require authentication for todo list
test_case_steps: Request GET /todos without an Authorization header or token.
expected_behavior: HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
